clue.text: Tons fed to big fat bird

indicators.note: something fed to another is put inside it, so the tons abbreviation goes into the other pieces

parts.note: OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize, big
rich food is fatty

explanation.surface: Feeding tons of food to a large, plump bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big fat' reads as a description of the bird, but each word is a separate piece, and 'fed to' puts the tons inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is the largest living species of bird.

clue.text: Unreliable character's part ending in tragedy

parts.note: a streak is a trait forming part of someone's character, as in a mean streak

indicators.note: the ending in a word is its final letter, here the close of tragedy

explanation.surface: An actor's role closing with a tragic flourish proves an untrustworthy figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Streaky is informal for erratic or inconsistent in performance, as a streaky batsman is.

clue.text: Discontinue Parliamentary sessions for withdrawing inferior plant

indicators.note: withdrawing a word means pulling it out of the longer word, leaving the remainder

parts.note: to prorogue is to suspend a parliament's sessions without dissolving it
pro means in favour of, for

explanation.surface: A government suspends Parliament to get rid of a weed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is not a link here: as PRO it is taken out of PROROGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners call a plant that differs from and falls short of its type a rogue and weed it out.

clue.text: Mission Impossible star runs warship

parts.note: Tom Cruise stars in the Mission: Impossible films
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A film actor famous for action roles commandeers a fighting ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruiser is a fast, medium-sized naval fighting vessel.

clue.text: Alternate fourth of horses dropping from disease at last

indicators.note: dropping from means a letter falls out of the word for the illness

parts.note: staggers is a disease of horses and cattle causing unsteadiness

indicators.note: the fourth of a word is its fourth letter, here in horses

explanation.surface: A ploy to rotate horses after one of them falls ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' says the S is dropped from the end of STAGGERS. 'Alternate' is a verb: to stagger shifts or hours is to arrange them alternately.
explanation.definitionFit: Staggering working hours means arranging them so they overlap or take turns rather than coincide.

clue.text: Dump favourite fur cape

parts.note: tip means to dump, as rubbish is tipped
a teacher's pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: Throw away the cape you liked best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dump' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A tippet is a woman's short fur cape or stole worn around the shoulders.

clue.text: My pocket's where I stuff any old thing

definitions.text: where I stuff any old thing

parts.note: my! and glory! are both exclamations of surprise
a pocket in billiards, or of air, is a hole

explanation.surface: Someone explains that their pocket is where they cram all sorts of junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive but is the exclamation, as in 'My, how you've grown!'
explanation.definitionFit: A glory hole is a cupboard, drawer or room where miscellaneous clutter is thrown.

clue.text: Get lean to become So?

indicators.note: one set of letters coming to be another word signals a rearrangement of them

explanation.surface: Slimming down is the way to look stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: As an &lit the whole clue is also the definition: shedding weight to become graceful, with So standing for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means graceful and stylish in shape, which a slimmer figure is held to be.

clue.text: Light regulator offering Italian shade

parts.note: a Venetian comes from Venice in Italy
a blind is a window shade

explanation.surface: A window covering made in Italy that keeps out the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A Venetian blind's slats tilt to control how much daylight enters a room.

clue.text: In recession one third off fermented milk food that may contain fruit

indicators.note: receding means going backwards, so the word is read from end to start
one third off means two of the six letters are cut

parts.note: yogurt is milk fermented by bacteria

explanation.surface: During an economic slump, a yogurt with fruit is reduced by a third in price.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove YO, a third of YOGURT, to leave GURT, and 'In recession' turns it round. The definition is cryptic: a TRUG is a shallow garden basket that may hold picked fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A trug is a shallow wooden basket used by gardeners for carrying produce such as fruit.

clue.text: Idle editor pursuing a French Master with cunning plan

indicators.note: one piece pursuing others comes after them, so the editor follows

parts.note: une is French for a, feminine
M is the abbreviation for master, as in an MA
a ploy is a cunning manoeuvre

explanation.surface: A lazy editor chases a French master teacher with a clever scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle can mean out of work, without a job.

clue.text: Snarls and rants about beginning to lose

indicators.note: one word put about another surrounds it, so the rants go round the letter

parts.note: to rave is to rant wildly

indicators.note: the beginning to a word is its first letter, here of lose

explanation.surface: Someone growls and shouts angrily as they start losing their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snarls' is a verb in the surface but means tangles in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To ravel is to tangle or entangle, as a knotted thread snarls.

clue.text: Ordinary number from Holly

definitions.meaning: a 1957 song by Buddy Holly, the American rock-and-roll singer

explanation.surface: A common song from the Christmas plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holly' looks like the festive plant but is Buddy Holly, and 'number' is a song.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everyday is ordinary and routine; it is also the title of a Buddy Holly single.

clue.text: What anorak perhaps does for fatigue

definitions.meaning: an anorak is British slang for an obsessive enthusiast such as a trainspotter, who watches a passing locomotive

explanation.surface: Asking what tiredness a raincoat does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anorak' is not a raincoat but the British slang for a geek, the classic case being a trainspotter: read the answer as two words, 'eyes train'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyestrain is tiredness or soreness of the eyes from overuse, such as long reading.

clue.text: Moons about, fast inducing sleep

indicators.note: the letters move about, rearranged into a new order

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: Wandering under the moon while fasting leads to drowsiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' is not speed here but the fasting season.
explanation.definitionFit: Somnolent means drowsy or causing sleepiness.

clue.text: Cherie's Dad's nipper given fresh start by Blair originally

indicators.note: a fresh start means the opening letter is replaced by another

parts.note: a tooth is something that nips

indicators.note: originally means the first letter, here of Blair

explanation.surface: Cherie Blair's father's young child is reinvented by Tony Blair at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Booth, an actor, was the father of Cherie Blair, wife of the former UK prime minister. 'nipper' looks like British slang for a child but is a tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: The actor Tony Booth was Cherie Blair's father.

clue.text: Imp decaudated seafood

indicators.note: decaudated means having had the tail cut off, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: scampi are breaded langoustines, a seafood dish

explanation.surface: A small devil has lost its tail, like a prawn being prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: A scamp is a mischievous child, a little imp.

clue.text: Wrap up or possibly freeze with cold for good

indicators.note: one thing with another for it is a swap, putting the cold letter where good was

parts.note: to congeal is to set or solidify, as freezing does
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Advice on whether to bundle up in winter or else freeze permanently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with cold for good' means replace G (good) with C (cold). 'for good' looks like 'permanently' but is part of the swap.
explanation.definitionFit: To conceal is to hide, as wrapping something up keeps it from view.

clue.text: Sporting wench stripped after December day's ultimate lewdness

indicators.note: after places the wench's remains following December

parts.note: someone sporting a hat is in a hat, wearing it

indicators.note: stripped means its outer letters are removed, leaving the middle
the ultimate letter is the last one, here in day's

explanation.surface: An undressed woman at a Christmas party at the end of the day suggests bawdy behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecency is behaviour offending against public decency, lewdness.

clue.text: Be more excited about a drop of water once put in shade

indicators.note: the anagram goes about the drop, enclosing it
excited letters are stirred up into a new order
a drop of a word is a tiny bit of it, its first letter

explanation.surface: Becoming more thrilled about a splash of water that once was put somewhere shady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks an archaic or literary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To embower is to enclose in a bower, a leafy shelter, as in older poetry.

clue.text: Colour of vehicle belonging to me

parts.note: a car is a road vehicle
mine means belonging to me

explanation.surface: Asking the colour of the car that is mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmine is a vivid crimson colour.

clue.text: Revises what happens at midday

definitions.meaning: at noon the morning, a.m., comes to a close

explanation.surface: Asking what edits happen at noon.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second definition as two words: AM ENDS, the morning finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend is to revise or correct; at noon the morning, a.m., finishes.

clue.text: Grass part of a lawn fit for ordinary wear

parts.note: British slang: to grass is to inform on someone to the police

indicators.note: part of signals that a few letters run inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Turf from part of a garden lawn suitable for everyday use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like a lawn plant but is the British slang verb for telling tales to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal clothing is casual dress suited to everyday occasions.

clue.text: Rhythmic work in first of overs by Harmison, maybe wicketless

indicators.note: wicketless means losing the wicket letter, W in cricket scoring

parts.note: Steve Harmison was an England fast bowler, an example of a bowler

indicators.note: first of means the opening letter, here of overs

explanation.surface: A cricket report: England's fast bowler takes no wickets in his first over.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls bowled by one player. 'maybe' marks Harmison as an example of a bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravel's Bolero is an orchestral piece built on a repeated Spanish dance rhythm.

clue.text: Where to get the usual train?

definitions.meaning: a nearby pub where a regular orders the usual drink
a stopping service serving every station on a line

explanation.surface: Asking where to catch the regular train.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain one's local is one's neighbourhood pub, where the barman pours 'the usual'.
explanation.definitionFit: A local is a regular's nearby pub, and also a stopping train that calls at all stations.

clue.text: When perhaps we're on hand

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Asking when we might be available to help.
explanation.definitionFit: Here and now means at this very moment, the present time.

clue.text: Extract a piece of jewellery

definitions.meaning: a short excerpt from a film or programme
an ornamental brooch fastened by a spring

explanation.surface: Removing a piece of jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A clip is a short excerpt from footage, and also a brooch or earring fastened with a clasp.

clue.text: Lead performer following backing player's piece is top group member

indicators.note: following places the leader after the reversed piece
backing means going backwards, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: a tile is a Scrabble or mahjong player's piece
the leading performer comes first, 1ST, written with I for the one

explanation.surface: A star singer follows a backing musician's track and becomes a member of a top band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like backing vocals but reverses TILE to ELIT. The 'top group' is the elite, the best.
explanation.definitionFit: An elitist belongs to, or favours, a select superior group, the elite.

clue.text: Basket Waitrose supply ultimately to carry bread?

definitions.text: Basket Waitrose supply ultimately to carry bread?

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it inside, so the bread goes within the final letters
ultimately means the last letters of the three words before it

parts.note: a roll is a small loaf of bread

explanation.surface: Shopping at Waitrose, a British supermarket, with something to carry the loaves.
explanation.walkthrough: As an &lit, the whole clue describes a supermarket trolley used to carry bread around Waitrose.
explanation.definitionFit: A supermarket trolley is a wheeled basket for carrying groceries such as bread.
